title: Items and inventory
summary: Move things between lists, and show them.

steps.title: Stage 3: things to pick up
body: Each room already has an `items` list. Now the player gets an `inventory` list, and two commands move items between the two.

This is the core of most programs: state that changes in response to commands, and output that reflects it. Keep each command in a small function (`take`, `drop`) so the loop stays a readable dispatcher.

answer: Taken key. There is no key here. There is no sword here.
steps.explain: Lists are mutated in place, so the second `take("key")` finds nothing. `"" or "nothing"` gives the fallback for an empty join.

steps.prompt: `case ("take" | "drop"), "":` comes before `case "take", item:`. Why does the order matter?
options: `item` would capture `""` too, so the specific case must come first
steps.explain: A capture pattern like `item` matches anything, including an empty noun. Match cases are tried top to bottom.

steps.title: Take and drop
prompt: Your stage 2 game is in the editor. Add items:
- `describe` prints `You see: a, b` (sorted) after the description when the room has items, before `Exits:`
- `take ITEM`: move it from the room to the inventory, `Taken ITEM.`, or `There is no ITEM here.`
- `drop ITEM`: move it back, `Dropped ITEM.`, or `You don't have ITEM.`
- `inventory` (or `i`): `You carry: a, b.` (sorted) or `You carry: nothing.`
`get` already means `take` thanks to your parser.
solution: "desc": "A dusty hall with a grand staircase.",
"desc": "Shelves of old books line the walls.",
"desc": "It smells of old bread. A trapdoor leads down.",
"desc": "Dark and damp. Something glints in the corner.",
words = [w for w in line.lower().split() if w not in FILLER]
